page: UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-128GB is a KVM-hypervised virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, operating on a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 500 GB of local SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3883.99 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 41.32 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 100920.97 and a PassMark CPU score of 56071.16. Memory bandwidth is also strong, measuring 235.89 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 118.27 GB/sec for large-block write operations. However, the server exhibits average performance in software compilation, text processing, and static web serving throughput, while LLM inference speeds for small models are weak to poor, with text generation limited to 31.14 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a balanced general-purpose profile. The inclusion of 500 GB of local SSD storage and strong database operations performance makes this server suitable for relational databases, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and general-purpose backend applications. However, the shared CPU allocation model may introduce performance variability under sustained, high-intensity compute workloads, and the lack of GPU acceleration makes it unsuitable for modern language model inference.
